title: AI infrastructure
summary: Connect AI components to familiar application and infrastructure controls.
html:
Objectives

  • Identify inference, administration, storage, and network boundaries.
  • Review secret handling and service identities.
  • Measure bounded resource use and request limits.

Concepts and boundaries

AI services still depend on HTTP endpoints, credentials, storage, networks, and administrative interfaces. Inventory public inference APIs separately from model-management APIs and internal orchestration services. The model’s behavior does not replace ordinary authentication, authorization, input validation, and patch management.

Resource consumption matters because prompts, retrieval, and tool loops can amplify work. Measure within a small explicit budget in your lab. A slow response alone is not proof of denial of service; distinguish queueing, token generation, retrieval latency, and downstream tool time. Vulnerability claims about a serving product must match the deployed version and configuration.

Open full-size diagram

Practice checklist

Use an isolated lab or an explicitly authorized environment. Record prerequisites and configuration before changing inputs.

  1. Inventory endpoints and versions in a local or authorized environment using its configuration and normal requests.
  2. Check which endpoints require authentication and whether a low-privilege lab account can reach administrative functions.
  3. Review logs and browser responses for synthetic credential leakage; use fake credentials for demonstrations.
  4. Run a small fixed number of benign requests at agreed sizes and record response time, token limits, and rate-limit behavior.
  5. For a known issue, read the vendor advisory and compare affected versions and prerequisites before attempting a lab reproduction.

Expected observations

Produce a map of reachable services, identities, and limits. Report observed configuration rather than inferring a product or vulnerability from a model’s self-description. Failed requests may show a correctly enforced control.

Mitigations and retesting

Isolate management interfaces, scope service accounts, rotate exposed credentials, patch serving dependencies, enforce request and execution budgets, and monitor unusual resource consumption. Keep test limits explicit to make results reproducible.
